refused_panel.scope_excerpt: the measured coverage holes of the 28-volume / 721-cluster run: vascular endothelium in retina and choroid, macrophage and monocyte separated from microglia, retinal rod depth, and the RPE/melanocyte pair

lensiris_increment.scope_excerpt: the two tissues that docs/TISSUE_COVERAGE_DECLARATION.md declares as gaps (lens, iris): the author-side class names that were absent from the vocabulary, carrying their own Cell Ontology terms

flag_spec.what_is_being_flagged: a gene, or an entry, whose basis for being in a shipped panel is an evaluation volume — i.e. the benchmark's own substrate — rather than independent literature or an in-house non-benchmark atlas
why_a_file_level_bit_is_not_enough: the same panel file mixes the three readings: measured per panel in ITEM4_EVAL_BASIS_BY_PANEL.tsv (columns A, B, C sum to the panel's gene count)
a panel whose declared selection basis is an evaluation volume still carries genes whose own entry names an independent source (reading C), so flagging the file would condemn them
a panel whose declared basis is independent can still carry an entry whose only provenance is an evaluation volume (reading B), so not flagging the file would exonerate them
what_the_flag_must_assert: granularity: per entry (label) inside a panel file, and per gene inside that entry — not per file
a basis class drawn from a closed vocabulary: independent_literature | independent_in_house_atlas_non_benchmark | evaluation_volume | evaluation_report_holes | unstated

when the basis class is evaluation_volume or evaluation_report_holes: the entry must carry an independent anchor (a PMID or a corpus row) for every gene it wants to be usable for a lineage/marker claim, named per gene — the flag says 'this candidate list leaned on the benchmark', not 'this gene is unusable'
the name of the evaluation artefact it leaned on (volume id / report id), so a reader can re-derive the exclusion list instead of trusting the bit
an explicit statement of what the flag does NOT claim: it does not assert that the gene is wrong, and it does not authorise changing a shipped panel body
flag_spec.where_it_must_be_enforced: at the consuming layer (the marker layer's admission test), not by editing the shipped panels: the contract's red line forbids deriving a marker from the evaluation volumes' own queries, and a rewrite of kb/ is an activation by another name
flag_spec.machine_check: for every assertion in a lineage artefact: if the source entry's basis class is evaluation_volume or evaluation_report_holes, the assertion must carry an anchor that is not derived from that volume; the marker layer already implements exactly this for reading A (the four-condition corpus test), and reading B is what is not yet checkable
flag_spec.status: registered here; not activated, and no panel body is changed by this card
